rows.title: Apollo chief economist says there’s ‘zero evidence’ AI is killing jobs—in fact, he says it’s creating them
rows.standfirst: Torsten Sløk, chief economist at Apollo, says AI will only create more jobs for human workers—even as companies tie their layoffs to the tech.

rows.title: As loyal Boomers win and job-switching Gen Zers lose, the labor market of 2026 reveals a decade of bad career advice
rows.standfirst: For years, the playbook was clear: don’t stay too long, always negotiate your next move, loyalty is for suckers. It hits different in “low-hire, low-fire.”

rows.title: Gen Z is losing the most in the AI economy—and Goldman warns it’s about to get worse
rows.standfirst: Goldman has good news on the AI job-killing story, until you look closely at the numbers.

rows.title: Buffett says Abel ‘has launched’ with his first big Berkshire deal: an $8.5 billion housing bet
rows.standfirst: The Taylor Morrison acquisition checks every box in Warren Buffett’s playbook—except one.

rows.title: ‘Nobody’s safe’: Cognizant projected 90% of jobs would be disrupted by 2032—but we’re beyond it 6 years early
rows.standfirst: Head of Research Ollie O’Donoghue said even plumbers aren’t immune to AI. “The plumber still fixes the pipe,” but AI can inspect and diagnose.

rows.title: Cognizant CEO is swimming against the tide on AI: he’s hiring over 20,000 graduates this year and says AI tokenmaxxing is a ‘vanity metric’
rows.standfirst: Ravi Kumar S., CEO of $27 billion IT firm Cognizant, says AI won’t kill entry-level jobs—and companies obsessed with tokens are measuring the wrong thing.

rows.title: It’s not a recession. But Goldman says your paycheck is acting like it
rows.standfirst: Real income growth has slowed to a pace “rarely seen outside of recession,” Goldman Sachs warns — and Americans are only beginning to feel the squeeze.

rows.title: Meet America’s ‘Disillusioned’: the 32% feeling betrayed and rejecting the establishment—and they’re not who you think
rows.standfirst: They work full-time, play by the rules and they still raid their retirement savings. The Roosevelt Institute looks at America’s economically betrayed.

rows.title: Teens are up against the worst summer job market in nearly 80 years—they’re fighting against hundreds to work at ice cream shops and swimming pools
rows.standfirst: High schoolers haven’t faced this tough of a summer job market since 1948. Rising inflation, higher oil prices, and a slow hiring market are to blame.

rows.title: New jobs report shows 7.6 million job openings added in April as layoffs and people quitting their jobs both fell
rows.standfirst: The Labor Department reported 6.9 million jobs in March and had forecasted only 6.9 million in April.

rows.title: AI may already be adding hundreds of billions to the economy—without showing up in the data
rows.standfirst: A new policy brief argues AI may already be adding hundreds of billions to the global economy—but official statistics aren’t built to see it.

rows.title: Data center CEO is hoping for a skilled-trades revival in his lifetime—he’s recruiting couch-dwelling Gen Z with two weeks of vacation on day one
rows.standfirst: The push to build AI may be reshaping work—but the resulting data center boom is also accelerating demand for hands-on labor, according to Dycom Industries CEO Dan Peyovich.

rows.title: Trade war is back on as White House floats a new minimum 10% tariff plan—with carveouts for coffee, beef, and microchip suppliers
rows.standfirst: “The proposed tariff exemptions for key foodstuffs seem to indicate that someone in the administration is aware of the way high-frequency purchases are shaping inflation perceptions.”

rows.title: Despite his hectic schedule, Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins says he’s ‘the most responsive person in the company’—and looks for the same trait in new hires
rows.standfirst: Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins prides himself on his rapid-fire replies, and looks to hire talent who are just as driven as him: “I try to set that pace for people.”

rows.title: AI was supposed to be killing jobs. In spring, the labor market is opening up instead
rows.standfirst: “The data doesn’t back it up,” says Employ America’s Skanda Amarnath, who sees backfilling behind a labor market that’s stabilizing.

rows.title: ‘A landmark moment for homebuying’: A San Francisco seller wants OpenAI or Anthropic stock for their $3 million home
rows.standfirst: As Anthropic and OpenAI race toward the public markets, a seller is betting that AI employees’ paper wealth is worth more than dollars.

rows.title: Scott Bessent says America’s in a ‘manufacturing renaissance,’ so where are the jobs?
rows.standfirst: He’s not alone. Apollo Global Management Chief Economist Torsten Slok thinks we’re living through an “industrial renaissance.”

rows.title: Gen Zers are more disconnected and distrustful of coworkers than their older colleagues—and they’re so lonely they’re taking days off work
rows.standfirst: Thanks to the pandemic, Gen Z workers missed out on the “in-office rituals”—and now they’re so isolated it’s hurting their careers.

rows.title: BofA on the ‘fundamental disconnect’ in the housing market: You’re blaming the wrong person for why you can’t afford a home
rows.standfirst: “Affordability is a key voter issue, but proposals to fix structural supply shortages are politically unpopular and lack short-term payoffs.”

rows.title: Trump promised deportations would protect American jobs. Brookings said ICE raids have cost the economy over 668,000 of them
rows.standfirst: A recent study from Brookings found that ICE arrests shocked local economies and drove unemployment.

rows.title: The May jobs report just blew past expectations—and maybe too far for markets
rows.standfirst: The labor market delivered 172,000 jobs in May, past the expectation for 88,000.

rows.title: NYU Stern professor Suzy Welch says the career aspiration to follow your passion is ‘dumb advice’
rows.standfirst: Suzy Welch, author and NYU Stern School of Business professor, says without the right talent or attitude, it’s hard to turn a passion into a career.

rows.title: One in five homebuyers is a single woman – here’s what’s driving the shift
rows.standfirst: Rising incomes, financial discipline and shifting life priorities are changing the market—even as affordability and hidden costs remain major barriers.

rows.title: This realtor is betting big on the AI IPO boom, but buying a house with stock will have to go through the OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s boards first
rows.standfirst: In a tight housing market, some Bay Area homesellers believe exchanging their houses for stock will benefit asset-rich tech workers. But those transactions are subject to board approval.

rows.title: This Gen Zer got reprimanded at Goldman for making cake videos as the ‘Investment Baker.’ She quit her job and is building a dessert empire
rows.standfirst: Allison Sheehan left her full-time job as a Wall Street wealth manager to scale her cake business, with a CPG brand on the horizon: Alleycat Baking Co.

rows.title: ‘The golden years are not golden’: Boomers are hoarding most of America’s wealth and power because they’re terrified of outliving their money
rows.standfirst: They followed the script—work hard, buy a house, save for retirement. Now millions of boomers feel trapped.

rows.title: Gen Zers are arriving at college unable to even read a sentence—professors warn it could lead to a generation of anxious and lonely graduates
rows.standfirst: With Gen Z students struggling to read, academics have been forced to adapt—a move critics describe as “coddling” the next generation of workers.

rows.title: Walmart CEO John Furner says even wealthy shoppers are now shopping at the discount grocery chain as high prices stretch six-figure earners
rows.standfirst: Walmart CEO John Furner says wealthy customers are shopping at the budget grocery chain as high prices stretch family finances to a breaking point.

rows.title: The AI trade’s worst day in a year became a buying opportunity by Monday
rows.standfirst: Friday’s Nasdaq rout looked like the start of a real repricing. By Monday, chipmakers were rebounding.

rows.title: Your career needs a ‘gym membership’ to keep up with continuous AI advancements, says Campus founder Tade Oyerinde
rows.standfirst: “I’m sorry if you’re exhausted,” said Campus founder and chancellor Tade Oyerinde.

rows.title: Gen Z hiring manager says boomer bosses are right about her generation’s ‘attitude’ problem after a candidate took the interview from her phone
rows.standfirst: “Gen Z aren’t getting jobs because of their attitude,” a Gen Z hiring manager slams after one applicant dialed in from their phone and demanded more money.

rows.title: Home sales are finally recovering and outpacing economists predictions even as mortgage rates remain high
rows.standfirst: Sales rose 3.2% compared with May last year.

rows.title: Around 22 million teenagers are making their pocket money on video games, online reselling, and in-game platforms like Roblox
rows.standfirst: The Gen Alpha are making money from their online hobbies and managing multiple streams of income from just 13 years old.

rows.title: Should Americans get an equity stake in AI? Trump and progressive Democrats float public ownership of AI
rows.standfirst: In an unusual cross-ideological convergence, Trump and progressive Democrats like Bernie Sanders are both floating some form of public equity in AI.

rows.title: Wall Street dumped nearly $1 trillion in tech stocks by midday—then clawed it back and bought peanut butter and paint
rows.standfirst: A midday rout in the “Parabolic 7” chipmakers reversed by the close as money fled into the market’s dullest corners.

rows.title: A ‘MAGA Warrior’ Texas ag chief is publicly blasting the USDA over a flesh-eating pest threatening America’s beef supply
rows.standfirst: The flesh-eating New World screwworm fly was found in Texas last week for the first time since 1966.

rows.title: Inflation is back above 4% for the first time since 2023—but Kevin Warsh might catch a break
rows.standfirst: Core inflation stayed tame, easing hawkish worries at the Fed.

rows.title: The architect behind Claude Code reveals the three things Anthropic looks for in a good hire—and why people with low ego are a must
rows.standfirst: Anthropic’s exec Boris Cherny reveals why being humble makes job applications stand out at the hottest AI company right now: “Ego just gets in the way of stuff.”

rows.title: A 5-week course and a guaranteed job: Meta commits $115 million to solve the skilled-trades shortage stalling its AI build-out
rows.standfirst: The investment is part of the company’s larger plan to spend $600 billion on its U.S. data center build-out by 2028.

rows.title: ‘I love the inflation’: Trump is ‘not concerned’ about inflation hitting 4% for the first time since 2023. ‘The numbers were great’
rows.standfirst: The president told reporters that the inflation number is only reacting to the war in Iran, and it will adjust once the ceasefire becomes permanent.

rows.title: Ken Griffin’s Citadel companies just hired 350 interns—only 0.36% of over 115,000 young applicants made the cut
rows.standfirst: Financial holding giant Citadel is recruiting more entry-level talent for its internship than ever before. It’s a welcome opportunity in a dire market for Gen Z.

rows.title: Inflation is roaring back globally, 2022 style. The Iran war is only half the problem
rows.standfirst: Europe, China and the U.S. are straining to meet the demands of the AI boom

rows.title: Walmart has a message for its 2.1 million workers: AI is going to improve your job, not take it: ‘Technology will power our future’
rows.standfirst: Walmart is already using AI to design clothes and coordinate trucks—but the $967 billion grocery chain says humans “will lead” the transformation.

rows.title: Gen Z fled San Francisco for Texas and Florida. Now they’re turning ‘welcomer cities’ into the next big tech towns
rows.standfirst: The next wave of the migration story is already underway, and it’s moving the innovation economy into unexpected territory.

rows.title: The Gen Z cofounder of $1.6 billion Whop says his platform has minted over 650 millionaires—he wants to make work fun and money worries obsolete
rows.standfirst: CEO Steven Schwartz says workers enjoying their jobs is a “foreign” concept to most, but hundreds are becoming millionaires by profiting from their passions on Whop.

rows.title: Boomers actually do hold most of the wealth and power. So why do they call it ‘whiny’ to point that out?
rows.standfirst: My inbox called Millennials whiny. The Federal Reserve, a field of social scientists and Aristotle disagree.

rows.title: AI job disruption is here. The problem may be compounded because nearly 75% of people don’t apply for unemployment benefits
rows.standfirst: Many don’t apply because they don’t believe they will be eligible for benefits.

rows.title: Jalen Brunson just led the Knicks to a historic win—and credits his NBA veteran dad’s work ethic for preparing him for the job
rows.standfirst: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson led the Knicks to victory, scoring nearly half the points in the game. And he credited his drive to his father, Rick Brunson.

rows.title: Iran emerges from war with its economy in free fall and inflation on some food items above 400%. If the regime doesn’t fix it, ‘there will be trouble’
rows.standfirst: “But even with aid, Tehran’s ability to manage its domestic woes will remain limited, and the internal pressures will build.”

rows.title: A ChatGPT prompt almost killed Ryan Serhant’s $50 million NYC penthouse deal. Here’s how he saved it
rows.standfirst: At Fortune Brainstorm Tech, broker Ryan Serhant explained how a chatbot nearly blew up a $50 million NYC penthouse sale—and why AI still can’t replace a human in high-stakes deals.

rows.title: The CEO of $3 billion Michaels tells young workers to quit daydreaming and take risks because ‘the universe rewards doing things in action’
rows.standfirst: Michaels CEO David Boone tells new grads that “the universe rewards doing things in action versus analyzing and thinking about things.”

rows.title: Trump turned the dollar into a foreign policy tool, and now risks undermining the currency’s extraordinary status, think tank says
rows.standfirst: The administration is turning emergency dollar lifelines into geopolitical favors. Economists say that bargain could come at a steep cost.

rows.title: The new problem for millennial parents in the Northeast: The million-dollar starter home
rows.standfirst: The first rung on the property ladder now costs seven figures in a record 242 cities, a new Zillow report shows.

rows.title: ‘I have nothing to lose’: Perplexity CEO says fear of failure is ‘the stupidest thing’ holding you back
rows.standfirst: When fear of failure strikes, Aravind Srinivas, the CEO of AI giant Perplexity, reminds himself that just having a job was once the bar for success.

rows.title: The affordability crisis is so bad that, for the first time ever, both mom and dad are working full-time in most American families
rows.standfirst: A new study from Pew Research found that more heterosexual parents are holding full time jobs, even as they’re expected to be more involved at home.

rows.title: Meet the CEO of US Polo Assn: He grew up in one of America’s poorest regions and now hosts Prince William and runs a $2.7 billion brand
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Polo Assn. CEO studied accounting when millennials and boomers were abandoning it—and it opened the door to a $2.7 billion career in luxury fashion.

rows.title: Teen summer employment is headed for its worst year since 1948
rows.standfirst: Challenger, Gray & Christmas projects record-low teen hiring this summer as inflation, cautious employers, and AI squeeze out entry-level jobs.

rows.title: Exclusive: Arizona senator warns ‘ghost jobs’ are warping labor data, presses Trump admin to investigate
rows.standfirst: Sen. Ruben Gallego sent letters outlining his concerns on Thursday to the Department of Labor and Federal Trade Commission.

rows.title: ‘Work-life balance is a lie’: TIAA’s CEO broke down at a bus terminal after a long work day, then found a better way to think about it
rows.standfirst: TIAA President and CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett now looks at her life as a “diversified portfolio” and says it’s set her up for success.

rows.title: Miserable K-shaped economy might actually be fading, as lower-income families bounce back, says Bank of America
rows.standfirst: “If this narrowing of the K is sustained, one explanation could be job growth broadening into more blue-collar sectors such as leisure and hospitality, construction and manufacturing.”

rows.title: Record revenues. Record profits. Record revenue per employee. The Fortune 500 is richer than ever—and employing fewer people
rows.standfirst: Corporate America’s hiring slowdown, explained in charts and data.

rows.title: The Great Recession’s missing children are finally bringing college’s financial crisis into sight. Welcome to the ‘enrollment volatility’ era
rows.standfirst: The children that weren’t born after 2008 are starting to show up in enrollment, or lack thereof. It’s pretty simple what happens when student go missing.

rows.title: Beef is becoming a luxury as prices stay at record highs. They likely won’t come down until 2028, says Farm Bureau
rows.standfirst: Beef prices could increase as much as 18.3% this year due to high demand and higher production costs.

rows.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says electricians and plumbers will be needed by the hundreds of thousands in the new working world
rows.standfirst: The $5 trillion tech CEO warns the future won’t be powered by tech bros—but rather the blue-collar workers.

rows.title: Former VP Kamala Harris says she went through a nine-hour interview to land the job—but she couldn’t escape ‘gold medal depression’ even when she won
rows.standfirst: Kamala Harris has made history as the first woman to take on the roles of San Francisco DA, California attorney general, and U.S. vice president—but no matter if she wins or loses, she’s always hit with emptiness.

rows.title: Ground beef is up 20% since last year. A parasite, a drought and a July 1 trade deadline could push it higher
rows.standfirst: The U.S. cattle herd is at its lowest point since the 1950s. Trump’s USMCA threat could make the beef price crisis permanent.

rows.title: Why men keep dropping out of the labor force: It starts in childhood, when kids see how males around them struggle, economists say
rows.standfirst: “Our findings suggest that experience effects can turn short-run declines in labor demand into long-run declines in labor supply.”

rows.title: South Korean chipmakers are being paid such massive bonuses it’s becoming an inflation problem for the central bank
rows.standfirst: The Bank of Korea is worried that a wage-price spiral is increasing consumer demand and pushing up prices.

rows.title: Americans are fleeing the U.S. at record rates—an ex-Google engineer who left India to build a $7.2 billion AI firm says they’re making a huge mistake
rows.standfirst: He left India for Silicon Valley, built two billion-dollar companies, and insists the U.S. “remains the land of opportunity” as Americans flee.

rows.title: A record 1 in 3 Gen Z and young millennials were still living with their parents in 2025—more than during the pandemic—despite most having a job
rows.standfirst: Around 70% of 25 to 34-year-olds who still live at home with their parents are actually employed.

rows.title: Texas and Charlotte used to build huge McMansions—now they’re copying the California design tricks they once mocked
rows.standfirst: The American Dream is getting smaller and more expensive than ever for homebuyers.

rows.title: The Fed is fed up with inflation and will bring down the hammer with a series of rate hikes this year, reversing earlier cuts, BofA says
rows.standfirst: “The Fed was willing to look through the tariffs, but it is losing patience after the latest round of supply shocks.”

rows.title: Tech companies dealing with data center protests locally are fighting a losing battle: Only 8% of opponents actually live near one
rows.standfirst: Data center opposition—and the AI backlash in general—is more about anxiety towards the future than experience in the present.

rows.title: As 93% of Americans lean on coupons to get by, Bed Bath & Beyond is splashing out $100K on a home renovation for their thriftiest shopper
rows.standfirst: Bed Bath & Beyond’s “Legendary Coupon Hunt” is underway, and the thriftiest shopper will get a $100,000 home makeover if they bring in the oldest coupon to date.

rows.title: Cursor’s 25-year-old CEO turned a Discord server into a talent pipeline to build his $60 billion SpaceX-backed AI company
rows.standfirst: Cursor CEO Michael Truell hired many of his employees straight out of a Discord server.

rows.title: The man who invented the Fed’s magic trick just died. His successor is about to try it again
rows.standfirst: Alan Greenspan’s closest colleagues see his fingerprints in the AI bet: “Hopefully, it won’t end the same way.”

rows.title: Trump claims consumers are being ‘gouged’ by gas companies and orders DOJ price probe, as Bessent warns U.S. must avoid ‘foreign choke point’
rows.standfirst: “Gasoline prices better start going down a lot faster than what I’m seeing!” Trump wrote.

rows.title: ‘Wipe out and change are different’: Amazon exec slams AI job apocalypse fears as he hires thousands of Gen Z grads
rows.standfirst: Matt Garman, CEO of Amazon Web Services, is rejecting predictions of an entry-level job bloodbath, as he hires thousands of Gen Z talent.

rows.title: Trump’s international student crackdown kicked off a domino effect that could shave nearly $500 billion off the economy
rows.standfirst: Half of America’s STEM workers with PhDs are foreign-born, a talent pipeline that is quickly drying up.

rows.title: Congress’s landmark housing bill could backfire on millions of renters
rows.standfirst: The bipartisan bill hopes to bridge the gap between high home prices and Americans desperate for affording housing. But the ban on institutional investors could take away rentals millions rely on.

rows.title: A big look at the state of housing in America: Boomers won’t sell, millennials can’t buy, and Gen Z gets to watch the whole thing sort itself out
rows.standfirst: A new forecast says housing supply will finally outpace demand by 2035. Congratulations to everyone who wasn’t born before 1997.

rows.title: Gen Z graduates are blaming AI for their unemployment woes when they should be looking somewhere else
rows.standfirst: While AI companies sow anxiety around their technologies, there’s evidence elsewhere of different economic factors actually driving employment challenges.

rows.title: TIAA’s CEO made $26,000 in her first job but still maxed out her 401(k). She has advice for Gen Z
rows.standfirst: TIAA CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett tells Gen Z to “max out” their 401(k)s before they get paid: “Because once you get it, you will find ways to spend it.”

rows.title: One U.S. college is fixing tuition at just 10% of parental income: ‘We’re not hiding the cost of college behind secret formulas’
rows.standfirst: At Whitman College, a private college in Walla Walla, Washington, what your parents earn each year will set the cost of your degree.

rows.title: U.S. companies swallowed the oil shock. They’re not sure they can do it again
rows.standfirst: A Fed survey of 530 executives found inflation now tops concerns for 25% of firms—nearly triple last quarter’s 9.5%—even as most have held the line on consumer prices.

rows.title: Trump turns on Big Oil donors who spent nearly $100 million to get him elected—now he wants the DOJ to investigate them for price gouging
rows.standfirst: Crude prices are back to prewar levels. Gas prices aren’t. Now Trump is pointing fingers at his own biggest donors.

rows.title: The bond market knows something about the $39 trillion national debt that Washington doesn’t
rows.standfirst: A more hawkish Fed could be bad news for the record debt. The bond market decided to ignore it.

rows.title: Congress just passed the most significant housing bill in decades, so why won’t Trump sign it?
rows.standfirst: Congress passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act 358-32 and 85-5 this week. Trump canceled the signing ceremony.

rows.title: Everyone agrees that you hate AI, but only Mark Cuban sees why Silicon Valley is powerless to fix it
rows.standfirst: “The big LLMs have lost the PR battle,” Cuban said. “Why? Because they all suck at putting people first.”

rows.title: Gen Z’s hiring hell is real: 1 in 3 employers admit they’re replacing entry-level roles with AI—and tech and manufacturing jobs are most at risk
rows.standfirst: AI is eating entry-level jobs fast. And a new survey of 600 recruiters shows an MBA may no longer be the escape hatch it once was.

rows.title: Stripe cofounder says Gen Z will need two college majors to compete thanks to AI—and investing legend Charlie Munger called it first
rows.standfirst: Stripe cofounder John Collison believes going to school and doubling up on disciplines with two majors is key to standing out in the AI era.

rows.title: One chart explains the economy’s terrible baby boomer hangover, Gen X’s invisibility, and millennial and Gen Z irrelevance
rows.standfirst: New Census data shows the 65+ population grew 16.2% since 2020 — nearly triple the rate of millennials — as younger generations scatter to exurban fringes.

rows.title: Job scams are getting more sophisticated, and they’re costing Americans millions
rows.standfirst: Nearly all scammers are using AI to track targets. It’s making the usual red flags harder to decipher.

rows.title: The 30-year fixed mortgage was supposed to be predictable. Two costs quietly broke that promise
rows.standfirst: A new survey shows 40% of homeowners said they’ve considered moving because their property taxes have gotten so high.

rows.title: Nobel laureate economist warns AI jobs apocalypse fears could become a self-fulfilling prophesy
rows.standfirst: “When millions of people make millions and millions of decisions based upon negative expectations, there is a risk that fear can actually help birth the reality.”

rows.title: ‘It’s not going away’: The Stanford economist who called the AI entry-level jobs crisis early has the receipts
rows.standfirst: Stanford’s Erik Brynjolfsson is partnering with ADP’s Nela Richardson on a live dashboard tracking what they found last summer: AI is eating entry-level work.

rows.title: The contrarian view for Fed rate cuts: Payrolls will weaken, inflation will plunge, and Kevin Warsh was ‘largely performative’ in his hawkishness
rows.standfirst: “He had to sound hawkish to draw a clear line between himself and the White House.”

rows.title: LinkedIn says real estate is one of the hottest industries for entry-level workers—One Gen Z sales agent made $75K his first year with no experience
rows.standfirst: Real estate is the second fastest-growing sector for new grads. With the right grit and self-determination, Gen Zers can earn into the six figures.

rows.title: Harvard’s housing report has a darker message than affordability—the middle-class home was always a historical accident
rows.standfirst: Harvard’s U.S. housing report points to an uncomfortable conclusion: homeownership is no longer something you earn. It’s something you inherit.

rows.title: The CEO behind Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t play video games, but analysts say he has put $1.5 billion behind the biggest game launch of the decade
rows.standfirst: “I don’t think being consumer-in-chief really helps a CEO be effective in this business,” said Take-Two Interactive Software CEO Strauss Zelnick.

rows.title: Target is starting to track employees’ unexcused lateness and absences with a points system—and if they rack up 12, they’re fired
rows.standfirst: Target staffers who clock in late and skip work enough to rack up 12 points will be shown the door. It’s just one way companies are tightening their grip on in-person attendance.

rows.title: Ford on why it hired 350 ‘gray beard’ engineers: you need their mentorship for younger workers — and to drive huge AI productivity gains
rows.standfirst: “These engineers carry the hard-earned wisdom of decades of design,” Ford told Fortune, adding that AI is important to quality gains.

rows.title: Remote-first fintech giant Revolut is making the office compulsory for new Gen Z grads—and they’ll earn flexibility like their peers after one year
rows.standfirst: Revolut is pulling back its remote-first perks for grads in 2027—but those who succeed in the program have a shot at the digital nomad lifestyle.

rows.title: It started with one viral influencer complaining about Russia’s economy. Now a record 60% of Russians are pessimistic about their country’s outlook
rows.standfirst: Russia’s economy has been remarkably resilient, but it could be losing one of its most vital resources: public trust.

rows.title: Gen Z and millennials aren’t convinced the American Dream exists anymore: Only 40% of them can afford to buy a home
rows.standfirst: Homeownership can still be a sound financial decision all around, but only for those who can afford it.

frame: Union of four fixed economic tags
